rv.q: It is an important play that should be seen.
That Howard Skora's latest World Premiere is as entertaining as a fact-based play can be is icing on the rainbow-colored cake.

Texas Sodomy wants to be a raucous comedy, courtroom procedural, domestic tragedy, history pageant, and inspirational drama at once. Skora, who also directs, has found no theatrical language capable of holding them together.
With Texas Sodomy , Howard Skora has created something genuinely special: a politically significant work of theater that succeeds first and foremost as compelling human drama.

cn.t: Critics largely praise this fact-based drama about the landmark Lawrence v. Texas case as wildly entertaining and a triumph of storytelling, though one reviewer finds it falls short of its subject matter's significance.
